fact: The Department of Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation says the Presidential Hotline received 339,579 cases since September 2009, including calls, emails and walk-ins, of which 242,636 were complaints, logged in a web-based ITSM system.
DPME says hotline complaints are assigned through ITSM directly to stakeholders, municipalities and departments, each with a licence to view and close cases.
DPME says 234,752 of 242,636 complaints (96.7%) were resolved as at 17 December 2024 and that quarterly, mid-year and annual hotline reports are available.
DPME says the Khawuleza app received no cases after being piloted in Limpopo owing to technical glitches, and benchmarking is under way for digitalising the hotline.
The Minister's reply says the Presidential Hotline received 1,832 complaints in the first quarter of 2025/26.
The reply says national and provincial departments are expected to resolve complaints assigned to them by the Presidential Hotline within 25 working days.
The reply says 991 of 1,832 complaints were resolved in the first quarter of 2025/26, a 55 per cent resolution rate.
The Mpumalanga Provincial Government said it would launch the Livi Lemphakatsi app on 30 April 2025, for residents to submit and track service delivery complaints.
